ctax.heading.text: The coordination tax sits between the floor and the record.

ctax.lede.text: Lots move faster, deviations surface during the run, and the batch record is already audit-ready.

ctax.sr.text: Four handoffs of production work, each compared side by side. Today each handoff is separated from the record by coordination work: one batch lives in four parallel records, matching the right checklist revision to the work order is operator memory, recall genealogy is assembled by hand in spreadsheets, and decision rationale leaves with the shift. On one governed record the same four handoffs stay connected: the record builds itself at the operation, the checklist arrives bound to the order at the right revision, genealogy is already linked as the lot moves, and the rationale is signed onto the batch. The metrics keep their original units and are not plotted on a shared scale.

ctax.stagecol.text: The same four handoffs, paid for twice

ctax.before.note.text: Production work is fragmented by the reconciling needed to match paper, systems, and memory.

ctax.after.note.text: Every operation, decision, and deviation stays attached to the same record.

ctax.stage1.note.element: Coordination tax · stage 1 after-note (batch record assembly)
ctax.stage1.note.text: Steps, consumption, and checks land as they happen.

ctax.stage2.note.text: The right revision arrives with the order. No memory required.

ctax.stage3.note.text: Inputs, parameters, and dispositions linked as the lot moves.

ctax.stage4.note.text: Who decided what, and why, signed onto the batch.
